quote: That was odd. That was for solar. I did do some type of estimate last week, but I didn't know that was for solar panels.
stewart_read: The customer reveals genuine confusion about what he previously signed up for — he doesn't recall it was specifically for solar panels. The rep never probes what he thought the estimate was for, which leaves a legitimacy gap unresolved and creates booking fragility going into the closer call.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may have judged the confusion as harmless small talk not worth slowing the call down for, prioritizing forward momentum toward the appointment.
coaching_implication: Manager should flag this as a spot where a 10-second clarifying question ('what did they tell you it was for?') would reduce the risk of the customer feeling ambushed when the closer shows up to talk solar.

quote: I'm kinda sold on it, but I ain't convinced her yet.
stewart_read: Customer discloses the real decision-blocker is his wife's buy-in. Rep does not argue this or try to overcome it as an objection, which is the correct protocol response.
coaching_implication: Reinforce this as the model move — the rep avoided the common mistake of treating spousal hesitation as something to win single-handedly.

quote: Okay. I mean, once I get her in advance, there'll be no problem.
stewart_read: Rep frames the meeting as the mechanism to bring the wife on board rather than trying to close the customer alone on the call, matching the correct protocol strategy.
alternative_hypothesis: A reactive read would say the rep dismissed the concern too quickly, but the follow-up at 03:25 shows this was a deliberate thread, not a brush-off.
coaching_implication: Good template line for training — 'once I get her in advance' reframes the appointment as the venue for spousal buy-in without arguing.

quote: Yeah. Well, that's what this meeting is for is to kinda explain to you guys both how it works and, you know, what the benefits are.
stewart_read: Rep explicitly says 'you guys both,' implying the wife should be on the call, but never directly asks the customer to confirm she will actually be present at 9 or 10 AM tomorrow.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may consider 'you guys both' sufficient confirmation without a direct ask, treating it as implied inclusion.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close this loop explicitly: 'Can you make sure she's free at that time too?' rather than assuming inclusion from phrasing alone.

quote: Yeah. I had a few guys come by with Iron Solar before, and and they told me how my house is positioned directly in sunlight. It is. I mean, it's on a Bitcoin lot and no trees blocking it.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a strong site-quality detail (corner lot, no shading) unprompted — a genuine positive signal for solar viability that the rep could anchor on.
coaching_implication: Rep let this pass without reflecting it back ('sounds like your home is a great candidate then') — a missed curiosity-building moment, though the call still moved forward to booking.

quote: That's a goal, man. If they can convince her, then I'm sure it's a goal. But
stewart_read: The booking is conditioned on the wife's buy-in happening during the appointment itself, not confirmed beforehand — this is a real, disclosed constraint rather than a procedural gap.
coaching_implication: Flag for the closer: the wife's presence and agreement is the linchpin of this deal, not a settled fact.

quote: I got you down for tomorrow at 10AM. So I'll send you a confirmation text with the, anytime of the meeting, and then we'll see you guys then.
stewart_read: The rep confirms day and time and promises a text, but never runs the 'is that fair?' handshake or the no-driving/computer instructions from button_up, leaving the confirmation procedurally thin despite the time being locked.
alternative_hypothesis: The short call length may reflect a rep who trusts the customer is already convinced and doesn't need the full button-up ritual — but the schema treats this as predictive of show rate regardless of rapport.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always run the fairness handshake and set expectations (sit down, no driving) even on calls that feel warm and fast.
